marks.gloss_en: תנן: ויש שטעון ברכה לפניו ואין טעון ברכה לאחריו. בשלמא לרב יצחק בר אבדימי לאפוקי ירקא, לרבי יצחק לאפוקי מיא, אלא לרב פפא לאפוקי מאי? -- if even water needs a blessing after, what is left for the mishnah's ויש?
whatever requires a blessing after it requires a blessing before it
לאפוקי מצות -- it excludes mitzvot (= p_lafokei_mitzvot)
[for Rav Pappa] it excludes mitzvot

ולבני מערבא, דבתר דמסלקי תפילייהו מברכי ״לשמור חקיו״, לאפוקי מאי? -- for the Westerners, who bless after tefillin, mitzvot are not excluded: what then does the mishnah's ויש exclude? (attacks the answer לאפוקי מצות; = p_bnei_maarava_lishmor_chukav)
the Westerners, after they remove their tefillin, bless 'who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to keep His statutes'
לאפוקי ריחני -- it excludes fragrances (= p_lafokei_reichanei)
it excludes fragrances
over an egg and kinds of meat, at the start one blesses 'by Whose word all things came to be'
Mar Zutra acted as Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi
Rav Ashi: I, when I remember, act as all of them
whatever is an egg's size -- an egg is better than it
אנא כאידך דרבי יצחק סבירא לי, דאמר רבי יצחק: אסור לאדם שיאכל ירק חי קודם ארבע שעות
Mar Zutra: I hold like the other [dictum] of R' Yitzchak -- that one may not eat raw vegetables before four hours
כי הא דביתהו דרב פפא בתר דמבשלא לה תברא לה בתמנן אופי פרסייתא -- as Rav Pappa's wife broke it with eighty Persian palm-sticks after cooking it
Rava to Rav Pappa: we break it [the turnip] with meat and wine
כרוב למזון אין ולרפואה לא? והא תניא: ששה דברים מרפאין את החולה... כרוב -- for sustenance yes and for healing no? but a baraita counts cabbage among six things that heal
אלא אימא: כרוב אף למזון -- read the clause as 'cabbage even for sustenance' (= p_kruv_af_lemazon)

the baraita: six things heal the sick of his illness and their healing is healing -- cabbage, beets, sisin water, honey, the stomach, the womb and the lobe of the liver (the prop encodes the clause the objection uses: cabbage heals)
איני?! והא אמר ליה רבא לשמעיה: כי חזית ליפתא בשוקא לא תימא לי במאי כרכת ריפתא -- is that so? Rava told his attendant to buy turnip whenever he saw it
Rava to his attendant: when you see turnip in the market, do not ask me 'with what will you wrap your bread?'
אמר אביי: מבלי בשר -- [the baraita speaks of turnip] without meat (= p_left_mibli_basar)
ורבא אמר: מבלי יין -- without wine (= p_left_mibli_yayin)
[the turnip is bad for the house] without meat
cabbage for sustenance
[spleen:] what is its remedy? let him chew it and throw it out
[leeks:] what is their remedy? let him boil them and swallow them
every raw vegetable makes pale -- R' Yitzchak: [that is] at the first meal after bloodletting
R' Yitzchak: whoever eats vegetables before four hours -- it is forbidden to converse with him
Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi were sitting; raw vegetables were brought before them before four hours; Ameimar and Rav Ashi ate and Mar Zutra did not eat
everything small makes small -- Rav Chisda: even a kid worth a zuz
every living thing restores the soul -- Rav Pappa: even the gildanei of the reeds
everything near the soul restores the soul -- Rav Acha bar Yaakov: the neck
a small salted fish sometimes kills -- on the seventh, the seventeenth and the twenty-seventh
Rav Idi bar Avin: [לצמאו comes] to exclude one whom a piece of meat choked
ומי איכא מידי דהוה שלק מזוני? -- is there anything that, boiled, is sustenance?
בקלח של כרוב שנו -- it was taught of a cabbage stalk (= p_kelach_shel_kruv)
Rav Ashi: they taught it of a cabbage stalk
